messages:
Jules: FYI we started seeing a latency spike on the 4.2.0 scheduler change. perfetto timelines show an extra 6-12ms gap in the tail of several requests after kernel selection changes. Not subtle.
Sam: Can you paste the perfetto capture link and the nsys snapshots? I can try a quick compare locally.
Jules: Perfetto: https://perfetto.dev/trace/rdw/2026/trace-248123.json (internal). Two nsys captures attached to build artefacts: before-change: s3://rdw-artifacts/prof/248120-before.nsys, after-change: s3://rdw-artifacts/prof/248123-after.nsys
Alex: Quick observation from the nsys timeline: after-change has repeated small memcpy kernels (~cudaMemcpyAsync) between attention kernels where before-change had a single chained memcpy. Looks like scheduler introduced a micro-reshuffle that breaks a batching-affinity assumption.
Miho: That matches my localized run. When the scheduler migrates a batch to a different CU for the second half of the request we pay an extra device-to-device hop. Kernel selector is choosing the same kernel variant but different stream/affinity -> extra sync.
perf-bot: automated-summary: after-change: +8.3ms p95, +12.1ms p99 for seq_len=1024, batch=1, NVTX hotspots around kernel:copy_back_async
Jules: Reproduction steps I used:
```
# checkout branch
git checkout main
git reset --hard 1f2a3b4c  # commit before scheduler tweak
# run perf harness
python infra/tools/run_inference_profile.py --model llama-7b --seq 1024 --batch 1 --profile nsys --out before.nsys
# then test after
git checkout 5e6f7a8b  # commit with scheduler change
python infra/tools/run_inference_profile.py --model llama-7b --seq 1024 --batch 1 --profile nsys --out after.nsys
```
Jules: bisect narrowed to range `1f2a3b4c..5e6f7a8b` and tests fail reproducibly on the tip. Need help isolating exact commit that causes memcpy splitting.
Sam: I ran `git bisect` locally for one pass. Found a likely suspect: commit `3c4d5e6f` touches runner scheduler handoff + stream assignment. The diff flips `stride_affinity=true` by default.
Alex: On the after.nsys I extracted kernel list (top kernels by time):
```
1. attention_fwd_v2 (35%)
2. cudaMemcpyAsync (12%)
3. kv_read_kernel (10%)
4. attention_bwd_v1 (8%)
5. cudaMemcpyAsync (6%)
```
Before-change cudaMemcpyAsync was a single combined 18% block between attention kernels, now it's split into two smaller calls with host-driven sync in-between.
Miho: Hypothesis: the scheduler's stream switch breaks the continuous pipeline that allowed the driver to coalesce D2D copies (or pinned buffer reuse). If we force `--scheduler.disable_affinity_swap` the after-change profile looks like before.
Jules: Can someone reproduce with perfetto so we can see thread/stream mapping? I can upload a short perfetto with NVTX overlays if useful.
Sam: I ran a short perfetto with nvtx markers, see heatmap: https://perfetto.dev/trace/rdw/2026/trace-248123-annotated.json. The stream lanes show a context handoff at the KV flush. The CSR on the second stream inserts a small barrier.
Alex: Minimal quick patch I tried locally: revert the line that flips stream id when `batcher->is_hot()` and instead keep sticky stream per request. After patch, memcpy consolidates. Will open a draft PR with benchmark numbers.
Jules: Can you paste the bisect log output you used? I want to re-run on CI.
Sam: Bisect snippet:
```
git bisect start
git bisect bad 5e6f7a8b
git bisect good 1f2a3b4c
# one session
Bisecting: 3c4d5e6f is the first bad commit
# 3c4d5e6f touched scheduler/runner/stream_assignment.cc
```
Miho: If we confirm `3c4d5e6f` then we need a longer-term fix: either make stream assignment idempotent for in-flight KV pages, or have the kernel selector emit explicit NVTX + stream affinity hints so the driver can avoid copies.
perf-bot: perf-ci: queued a dedicated nsys/regression job for commit 3c4d5e6f across seq_len 512/1024/2048. Expect artifacts in ~45m.
Jules: I created a small micro-repro harness: `infra/tools/stream-drift-repro.py` that simulates the short handoff with synthetic KV loads. It reproduces the extra memcpy reliably. I'll add to the PR and link.
Alex: Flamegraph link for after-change: https://rdw-graf/graph/248123-flame.svg — you can clearly see the split copy stacks.
Sam: Temporary mitigation for Dedicated: we can roll back scheduler default or expose `scheduler.affinity_swap=false` flag in runtime config; ops may toggle until we land a fix.
Miho: I'll prototype a change to make stream assignment stable for KV-backed tensors and run the perf job locally tomorrow AM.
Jules: Great. I'll wait for perf-ci results, then we'll decide revert vs targeted change. Thanks all :thumbsup!
Miho: ACK, will follow up with PR and attach updated nsys captures once ready.
thread_summary: Jules reports a latency regression after a scheduler change that caused stream/affinity handoffs and split cudaMemcpyAsync calls; team bisected to a scheduler commit, shared nsys/perfetto captures, repro steps, and proposed mitigations (sticky streams or flags). perf-ci queued a job to confirm.
